## Findings
- claim-1: The reported computational verification range is \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-6@L46-L54|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: For \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), the parameters are \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), and each proposed family has \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\) generators. [source-6@L18-L42|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-3: Put \(q=n-r\). For nonempty rectangular data \(i,j\ge1\), \(N>1\) holds exactly when \[ 1\le i\le q-1,\qquad 1\le j\le r-1. \] Indeed, \(b\ge1\), while \(a\ge1\) exactly under these two strict inequalities; then \(\binom{a+b}{a}\ge2\). If \(i=q\) or \(j=r\), then \(a=0\) and \(N=1\).
- claim-4: Interpreting “immediately beyond” as enlarging the tested rectangle to \(r\le5,\ q\le6\), the admissible new parameter instances with \(N>1\) are: \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c} r&q=n-r& (i,j)&\#\\ \hline 5&2,3,4,5,6& 1\le i\le q-1,\ 1\le j\le4&4(q-1)\\ 2,3,4&6& 1\le i\le5,\ 1\le j\le r-1&5(r-1) \end{array} \] Equivalently, these are \((r,n)=(5,7),(5,8),(5,9),(5,10),(5,11)\) and \((2,8),(3,9),(4,10)\), with the indicated \((i,j)\). The overlap \((r,q)=(5,6)\) occurs only in the first row. There are \(60+30=90\) such \((r,q,i,j)\)-instances.
- claim-5: The two Schur generating families are minimal for each of these 90 instances; this is not established by their enumeration.
## Strategy
Fix \(q=n-r\) and interpret “immediately beyond” as
\[
\{r\le5,\ q\le6\}\setminus\{r\le4,\ q\le5\},
\]
including the corner \((r,q)=(5,6)\). For rectangular Schur data \(i^j\subseteq q^r\), impose
\[
1\le i\le q-1,\qquad 1\le j\le r-1,
\]
which is equivalent to \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}>1\). This yields the conditional list of 90 \((r,q,i,j)\)-instances recorded in claim-4.

Keep this explicitly an enumeration of rectangular Schur-data instances until a sourced correspondence with admissible \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) is supplied.

## Gaps
- “Immediately beyond” is a convention; other boundary-expansion conventions give different finite lists.
- No grounded map from \((r,q,i,j)\) to \((r,s,t,n)\), nor its admissibility conditions, is presently available. Thus the 90 entries are not yet established as a bijective list of bigrassmannian permutation cases.
- Minimality of either Schur generating family remains conjectural for all newly listed instances.

## Next
- Obtain and verify the parameter correspondence between \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) and \(i^j\), including all constraints on \(s,t\).
- Translate the 90 rectangular instances into admissible \(v_{r,s,t,n}\)-cases, removing duplicates if the correspondence is not injective.
- For any selected cases, compute the indecomposable quotient presentation and retain minimality conclusions only when independently established.
